title: Refusal
description: The body of a refusal the control plane answers a request of the provisioner contract with, application/json, as the integration contract's refusal, https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/refusal.schema.json. The codes the starter meets: 401 unauthorized, one uniform unsigned answer for everything about who is asking, for each cause that refusal lists, a replay under the replay rule of https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/definitions.schema.json among them: it tells the starter nothing about which cause applied, and the starter never takes it as the pool's access key being revoked; 403 forbidden, a request outside the key's rights, a claim whose pool_id is not the key's node pool, and a request naming a dispatch_id that is unknown or of another node pool than the key's, each with the same signed body as an unknown id, so nobody learns whether an id exists: the signature with the pool's access key and this check authorise a request, not the id, and the control plane decides it before any 409 or 410; 400 bad_request, for two causes alone: a signing header sent twice, X-Qory-Access-Key-Id, X-Qory-Instance-Id, X-Qory-Signature-Ed25519 or X-Qory-Timestamp, or an X-Qory-Instance-Id that is absent or outside its pattern; 400 unsupported_contract_version, an X-Qory-Contract-Version that is missing, sent twice, not a decimal integer, or a revision the control plane does not serve; 400 invalid_request, a body that breaks its schema, an integer written with a fraction or an exponent, or an object that repeats a member, at any depth; 404 not_found, a route the control plane does not serve; 413 payload_too_large, a request over 1 MiB; 415 unsupported_media_type, a POST whose Content-Type is not application/json, while a GET carries no body and no Content-Type and is never refused 415; 409 no_gateway, a claim whose run's pool choice resolves to no gateway, or a handover at which the node pool has no gateway the run could be registered through, because the node pool is direct, it has no default gateway, its named gateway is not serving, or the gateway its choice resolves to has no active access key; after it the dispatch stays claimed until its lease lapses, as handover.schema.json describes; 409 handed_over, a second handover, since a run key is handed over at most once per run; 409 not_dispatched, a handover before dispatched; 409 lease_expired, a dispatched or a handover after the lease lapsed and the dispatch, not yet handed over, went back to the queue with the same run and has not ended, on which the starter stops the job it started for that dispatch; 410 gone, a request naming a dispatch that ended: before its handover, because its work item was closed or undone, or after its handover, with its run, since closing or undoing the work item after the handover does not end the dispatch at once and the run goes on to its end; 429 rate_limited, with Retry-After, the seconds the starter waits before it sends the request again, built anew, as https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/definitions.schema.json describes a retry. A release after the handover, while the run goes on, is not refused: it is answered as a success, the signed 204, and ends the run. A handover's refusals apply in the order handover.schema.json gives. No refusal is tied to a step or to a policy. A 401 is always unsigned. A 413, 415 or 400 bad_request may be unsigned, because the control plane may decide them before it verifies the request's signature. Every other answer is signed, and the starter acts on no other unsigned answer. On an unsigned 401, 413, 415 or 400 bad_request, the starter changes no state: no cursor, no run, no key. It treats the request as failed and sends it again, built anew as https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/definitions.schema.json describes a retry, with backoff. It never takes a 401 as revocation, and never splits or drops items because of an unsigned 413. An unsigned 429 is not a 429: the starter ignores its Retry-After and backs off as it does for any failed request. A member this schema does not define is refused.
